summary: Streaming SSE sessions stall mid-generation when canary rollout causes model warm-up delay
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports streaming (SSE) chat sessions that produce initial tokens but then enter a silent stall mid-generation when we are performing a canary model rollout. The stall lasts 30–90s and often recovers with the client receiving the remaining tokens in a burst, or the connection ultimately closes with no final chunk.

Impact:
- Affects multiple sessions for a single enterprise customer (NimbleHealth) using dedicated capacity in us-east-1.
- User-facing streaming hangs during live chat flows, causing timeouts and poor UX.
- Observed during planned canary rollouts and when routing shifts traffic from old model to canary variant.

Environment:
- Production, dedicated pool (dedicated-nyc-pool-7) serving NimbleHealth.
- Canary rollout configured: 5% traffic to canary before automatic ramp.
- Affected model families: redwood-v2-chat-8k (quantized) and fallback to llama3-13b-chat.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger a canary rollout for a chat-capable model in prod (example: increase canary to 5-10% via console).
Send a long streaming chat request that includes a ~2k token context and expects a multi-paragraph response using SSE client.
Observe token stream: initial tokens are received, then streaming pauses for 30-90s (silent period).
After delay either a burst of buffered tokens arrives or stream terminates with a 499/502 from gateway or client timeout.
Reproduce reliably when the canary routing decision causes some requests to be routed to a worker that is still performing model warm-up or KV cache priming.

investigation_notes: 03/10 14:20 - Support triage: customer-sup reproduced with NimbleHealth traffic pattern; correlated with canary ramp activity in deployment logs.
03/10 15:05 - Observed pattern: streaming stalls map to requests routed to new canary workers that had a KV cache miss and were performing quantized model kernel lazy-initialization.

03/10 16:30 - API gateway logs show silence (no chunk sent) during model warm-up window; gateway connection health-checks allowed connection to remain open but client-side timeouts occur in some SDKs.
03/11 09:12 - SRE reproduced locally by forcing worker to simulate 40s model initialization in serving-runtime; SSE client showed identical silent window.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-10T14:25Z]: Customer reported multiple incidents during today's rollout. Asked for priority escalation and logs. Attaching sample request id=abc123.

Diego Morales (SRE) [2026-03-10T15:10Z]: Reproduced locally by toggling canary routing. Hypothesis: lazy kernel init + KV cache priming on quantized workers delays first token flush. Investigating whether runtime buffers until model ready and then flushes as a burst.

Maya Li (Runtime Eng) [2026-03-10T17:02Z]: Found worker code path that suppresses SSE flush calls until token generation buffer hits a threshold when model is in 'initializing' state. Opening PR to force periodic flush during warm-up: linked PR #2147.

Diego Morales (SRE) [2026-03-11T09:40Z]: Temporary mitigation applied: reduce canary traffic to 0% for NimbleHealth and enabled warm-up preloading for quantized variants in the dedicated pool. Customer notified of mitigation.
NimbleHealth (Customer) [2026-03-11T10:05Z]: Appreciated the quick mitigation; reported fewer stalls after reroute. Asked for permanent fix and postmortem.
root_cause: A combination of canary routing to freshly provisioned quantized workers and a runtime optimization that deferred SSE chunk flushes during kernel lazy-initialization and KV cache priming. This created silent windows while the worker completed warm-up, leading to client-side timeouts or upstream connection resets.
workaround: 1) Roll back canary (set canary to 0%) for affected customers until fix is deployed. 2) Enable pre-warming for quantized model variants in dedicated pools (provision warm workers before routing traffic). 3) Increase client-side SSE keepalive/timeouts temporarily.
resolution_notes: Merged runtime fix to flush partial token buffers periodically during worker warm-up (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2147). Deployed to canary cluster 03/12; observed immediate reduction in SSE stalls during subsequent rollouts. Also added a rollout checklist item to pre-warm quantized workers and an automated health probe to detect long warm-up windows.
postmortem_follow_up: Action 1: Add an orchestration step to pre-warm at least 2 workers of any canary model variant before shifting traffic (owner: infra/serving, due: 2026-03-20)
Action 2: Add metric 'worker_warmup_duration' and alert if > 15s for any worker in production (owner: observability, due: 2026-03-18)
Action 3: Update rollout runbook to include SSE behavior note and rollback thresholds for streaming endpoints (owner: ops, due: 2026-03-17)
Action 4: Customer follow-up: provide NimbleHealth with postmortem and recommended client-side timeout defaults (owner: CSM, due: 2026-03-15)
